jamie_support: FYI customer (acct: ACME-42) reports sudden p99 spike to ~3s for chat completion over last 2 hours, started after a burst of long sequences. They see repeated OOM-ish logs and many retries. attaching snippet below. can runtime take a look? :eyes:

ravi_oncall: can you paste the tenant id + example request? also any correlation with model/route?

jamie_support: tenant_id=acme-42-prod, route=/v1/chat/completions, model=rwd-2x-large-quant, batch_size typical=8 -> burst to 32 for some jobs. snippet: ```ERROR: gpu_alloc: failed to reserve 24576KB (out of slab) at alloc.cc:312
WARN: kv_cache: growth triggered eviction loop (evict_count=0)
INFO: retrying request after soft-fallback to slower path (latency +1.2s)```

lee_runtime: thanks. looks like classic KV growth + slab fragmentation under bursty long-context workloads. quick triage: 1) are these requests using full prefix caching? 2) request seq lens? 3) is compaction/evict daemon running on those hosts?

jamie_support: customer says they disabled prefix caching for now due to correctness concerns. typical seq len for spike ~1500 tokens (mostly system + long user). compaction appears enabled per config but runs at default cadence.

ravi_oncall: immediate mitigation options: 1) enable active fallback routing for acme-42 to rwd-2x-medium-quant (lower KV footprint) for 30m 2) temporarily raise slab_compact_freq to 30s on their shard 3) set allocator hint `alloc_tuner=aggressive` for their pod to prefer larger contiguous allocations. any objections? :question:

lee_runtime: agree w/ that order. also add `kv_evict_threshold=0.65` (was 0.8) to force earlier trimming of per-tenant KV. watch for quality regressions if they drop model.

anna_custsuccess: looping in customer: would prefer non-model-change path first. they asked what the root cause is — can we explain simply?

lee_runtime: short explainer to send them: "Long sequences cause large per-request KV cache growth. On GPUs with fragmented slab allocs, the allocator can fail to find contiguous chunks even tho free memory exists -> triggers retries/slow path or soft-fallbacks. Over time per-tenant KV growth + default eviction thresholds let the tenant's working set inflate until we hit allocation pressure and degraded p99s."

jamie_support: customer agreed to let us change infra flags for short window. applying active fallback + kv threshold change now. will monitor.

enginfra-bot: deploy initiated: route-change acme-42 -> rwd-2x-medium-quant (canary 20%) by jamie_support @ 6357924350

ravi_oncall: while that rolls, can runtime produce a short heatmap of slab free vs contiguous runs for the affected hosts? need to validate fragmentation hypothesis.

lee_runtime: running quick probe:`/ops/tools/slab-inspect --hosts hostpool-3 --filter tenant=acme-42 --out /tmp/acme-frag.json` results: contiguous-run histogram shows >60% small runs <64KB, total free >30% but fragmented. upload shortly.

jamie_support: can we also try an immediate smaller change: `kv_shrink=true` per-tenant to be aggressive about freeing cold KV?

lee_runtime: yes `kv_shrink=true` + `kv_evict_threshold=0.65` + `slab_compact_freq=30s` is our short-term recipe. i'll make a playbook entry for this tenant and roll it if the canary looks good.

anna_custsuccess: customer asks for repro steps so their devs can avoid triggering it: any recommended client-side best practices?

lee_runtime: recommended client-side mitigations: 1) trim context where possible 2) send shorter anchor prompts and fetch more via streaming 3) enable prefix caching (we'll help validate correctness) 4) throttle concurrent long-context batches (limit concurrency to 4 for long seqs)

jamie_support: monitoring: created temp grafana panel for acme-42 p95/p99, slab_free_runs, kv_size, alloc_fails. alert if p99 > 1.5s or alloc_fails > 5/min.

enginfra-bot: alert rule created id=rule-ACME42-01 by jamie_support @ 6357924520

ravi_oncall: update: canary routed 20% -> p99 dropped from 3.1s -> 1.4s within 5m. alloc_fails reduced. looks promising. keep rolling to 100% over next 10m unless regressions. :thumbsup:

jamie_support: rolled to 100% at 6357924800. customer says UX improved. leaving flags in place for 1h then revert and re-evaluate with runtime for more permanent config/allocator tuning.

lee_runtime: follow-ups for next week: - analyze fragmentation causes and improve slab compaction heuristics - test a KV background shrinker that prioritizes cold keys - consider making `kv_evict_threshold` adaptive by tenant pattern - benchmark `alloc_tuner=aggressive` tradeoffs on perf/throughput

anna_custsuccess: customer thanks team, asked for a short RCA and timeline for permanent fix. i'll draft and share once we have the postmortem notes.

jamie_support: thanks all — marking thread resolved for now. plz add any findings to the incident doc. :white_check_mark:
